text: Ninsun did not repeat the question. She waited, allowing Zik to reconstruct the moment without offering words he might borrow. He closed his eyes and saw the chamber in fragments: torchlight unsteady across the carvings, the journal open in his hands, Enhedu near the threshold, Balag cursing under his breath. The fourth mark had not entered the wall. That was what troubled him now. He remembered no incision, no shadow forming along an edge.

text: The return felt longer than their departure. No new turn had appeared, yet the walls seemed to resist recognition. A crack Zik remembered passing on his right was now on the left. Moisture ran against the slope in several places, climbing the stone before slipping into the ceiling. Balag marked each junction with charcoal, though the black strokes faded almost as soon as the torch moved away. He stopped commenting after the second mark disappeared.
speaker: Narrator

text: When they reached the chamber, the darkness withdrew from its entrance in a slow vertical line, revealing the wall as though a curtain had been drawn aside. The three old carvings remained where they had been. Above them, the unfinished fourth mark waited in pale stone, unchanged in shape and position.

text: She unfolded a square of cloth across the floor and arranged her instruments upon it: measuring rods, waxed cord, charcoal, a small bronze pick, two tablets, and a brush worn almost to the binding. The familiar tools looked absurdly ordinary beneath the City's living walls. That ordinariness steadied Zik more than the torch. Ninsun was not preparing a ritual. She was setting up an excavation.
